plan.contextChunk: This figure shows two doubly linked lists and a free list sharing one set of arrays, drawn as a shaded three-row table beside three head pointers. At the left, three labeled boxes give the heads: "free" in a black box holding a white 10, "L2" in a medium gray box holding 9, and "L1" in a light gray box holding 3. To the right sits a black panel with columns numbered 1 through 10 across the top and three rows labeled in italics down the left side: next, key, prev. Every occupied cell is shaded to match the list that owns it. The medium gray cells at indices 9, 7, 1, and 5 carry keys k9, k7, k1, and k5, their next entries reading 7, 1, 5, and a diagonal slash for nil, their prev entries reading slash, 9, 7, and 1. The light gray cells at 3, 6, and 2 hold k3, k6, and k2, with next entries 6, 2, slash and prev entries slash, 3, 6. The black slots at 4, 8, and 10 hold only next values, 8, a slash, and 4, their key and prev cells left empty and cut by dotted white rules. Shading alone separates three structures interleaved across the same index range, and the free chain 10, 4, 8 shows that a slot on the free list needs just one link.

interactionPlan.concept: Multiple linked lists and a free list can share the same parallel arrays because each list is defined by pointer fields, not by contiguous storage locations.

demo_steps.title: One storage area, three structures
demo_steps.narration: The same indices 1 through 10 store records for L₁, records for L₂, and unused slots on the free list. Color shows current membership, while the head boxes identify where each chain begins.

demo_steps.title: Trace a list by following next
demo_steps.narration: Click free, L₁, or L₂ to highlight its indices in pointer order. The physical columns are interleaved, but the next fields recover the logical sequence.

demo_steps.title: Inspect an individual pointer
demo_steps.narration: Hover over a next or prev cell to highlight the index it names. A diagonal slash highlights nil, showing where a list begins or ends.

demo_steps.title: Allocate a free slot
demo_steps.narration: Advancing to allocation removes index 10 from the free chain and inserts it into L₁. Only the free head, the new record at index 10, and the neighboring L₁ pointer fields need to change.

demo_steps.title: Return a record to the free list
demo_steps.narration: Advancing to free removes index 9 from L₂ and makes it available again. The slot changes ownership, but the array table itself is not compacted or rearranged.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: In an array implementation of linked lists, list membership is determined by stored indices in pointer fields, so allocation and deletion reuse slots without moving records.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the figure as a wide three-row array table with columns 1–10 and head boxes on the left. Use black for free-list slots and the free head, medium gray for L₂, and light gray for L₁. Keep the records visually interleaved: L₂ follows 9 → 7 → 1 → 5, L₁ follows 3 → 6 → 2, and free follows 10 → 4 → 8. Use large serif italic math styling for labels and keys, diagonal slashes for nil, and dotted white rules across the empty key and prev cells of black free-list columns. For the allocation state, show index 10 becoming light gray and inserted at the head of L₁; for the free state, show index 9 becoming black and linked into the free list, with updated cells briefly emphasized rather than redrawing the whole table.

discrepancies: The generated figure is displayed much smaller than the source because a large right-side control panel occupies about half the viewport, reducing its effectiveness as a drop-in replacement for the static figure.
The italic 'free' label is placed too close to the black head box and appears to touch or slightly collide with it, whereas the source has clearer separation.
Several labels and cell contents are slightly smaller/thinner relative to the source, especially the key subscripts and row labels, making the figure less legible at inline size.
evaluation.notes: The array layout, colors, pointer values, free-list cells, and head boxes closely match the source, but the UI panel and slight label-spacing issues reduce static drop-in fidelity.
action_items: Dock the UI below the figure or make it more compact so the default figure occupies most of the available width like the source image.
Move the 'free' label slightly farther left from the black head box to avoid visual collision.
Increase or slightly embolden the row labels, key labels, and subscripts so they match the source's readability at inline size.
